title: RPC, gRPC and choosing REST vs RPC

kcs.statement: RPC exposes actions as remote function calls (e.g. sendMessage(userId, text)); a client stub serialises the arguments so the call looks local, though it can fail or time out over the network.

gRPC is an RPC framework that encodes messages with Protocol Buffers (a compact binary format) over HTTP/2 and supports streaming; it is common for internal service-to-service calls but needs a proxy for browser clients.

Public APIs used by third parties usually choose REST for its uniform, cacheable HTTP semantics, while internal, high-volume calls between services often choose RPC for lower overhead and typed contracts.

problem_ideas: Choose REST or gRPC for: a public weather API, orders-to-inventory calls at 50k/s, a mobile app backend.
A JSON payload is 1.2 KB and the protobuf version 300 bytes; estimate bandwidth saved at 20k calls/s.
Write the same 'send message' operation as an RPC signature and as a REST endpoint.
An RPC call looks like a local function; list three failure cases a local call never has.
Why can't a browser call a gRPC service directly, and what sits in between?
Design a streaming RPC for live driver location updates.
